extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining statutory bars and prior-art dates under the pre-AIA versions of 35 U.S.C. 102(d) and 102(e), including what counts as a foreign patent/reference, how to determine effective prior-art dates, and examiner search/benefit-claim procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-application-filed-more-than-12-months-before-US-effective-filing-date (102(d) requirement A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreign application must be filed more than 12 months before the effective U.S. filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should search for an issued foreign patent only if there is a reasonable possibility that a foreign patent covering the same subject matter was granted to the same inventive entity before the U.S. effective filing date. The anniversary date falling on a weekend/holiday extends to the next business day (Ex parte Olah). See MPEP § 2139.01 for effective U.S. filing date determination when subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-and-U.S.-applications-filed-by-same-applicant-or-legal-representative-or-assigns (102(d) requirement B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreign and United States applications must have been filed by the same applicant or by the same applicant's legal representatives or assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a U.S. application lists multiple inventors, priority may be claimed from separate foreign applications filed by subsets of inventors (e.g., one foreign app to inventor A and one to inventor B). Examiners must verify identity/ownership chain of inventive entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-application-actually-issued-as-patent-before-US-filing-date (102(d) requirement C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreign application must have actually issued as a patent or inventor’s certificate before the filing in the United States; it need not be published but the patent rights granted must be enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘‘Patented’’ requires a formal bestowal of patent rights (In re Monks). A published application generally is not a 'patent' for 102(d) (Ex parte Fujishiro; Ex parte Links), but an allowed application published for opposition that gives substantial provisional enforcement rights (e.g., German Auslegeschrift) can be treated as a 'patent' for 102(d) as of the publication for opposition (Ex parte Beik). The critical date is when the foreign patent becomes enforceable (issued/sealed/granted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-invention (foreign patent must involve same invention) (102(d) requirement D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The same invention must be involved — the application claims in the U.S. could have been presented in the foreign patent; the foreign patent must support the subject matter of the U.S. claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims need not be identical or in same statutory class; if the foreign specification fully discloses the invention and would have supported the U.S. claims, the 102(d) bar applies (In re Kathawala). A foreign patent that discloses aspects of the invention can bar U.S. claims even if the foreign claims differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search-for-pre-AIA-102(d)-prior-art
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should search for an issued foreign patent to use as pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) prior art only if there is a reasonable possibility that such a foreign patent exists and was granted before the U.S. effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches may be done on electronic databases by the examiner or STIC staff (see MPEP § 901.06(a)). The document must be a patent or inventor's certificate, not merely a published/laid-open application. If reasonable basis exists, examiner may require information under 37 CFR 1.105. Consider foreign pendency variation between countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anniversary-date-on-weekend-or-holiday-extends-to-next-business-day
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. application filed on the 1-year anniversary of the foreign filing prevents a 102(d) bar; if that anniversary is a Saturday/Sunday/federal holiday, the year is extended to the following business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule changes requiring deposit date attribution (e.g., Priority Express Mail®) do not affect applicant’s concurrent right to defer filing until next business day when last day falls on weekend/holiday (Ex parte Olah).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-in-part-breaks-chain-of-priority
rubrics_metrics.description: If a continuation-in-part (CIP) is filed and its claims are not entitled to the U.S. parent's filing date, the CIP's effective filing date may break the chain of priority to both U.S. and foreign parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If foreign application issues before the CIP filing date, the foreign patent may be used in a pre-AIA 102(d)/103 rejection against the CIP if the added subject matter does not render the claims nonobvious over the foreign patent (In re Van Langenhoven; Ex parte Appeal No. 242-47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure-without-claiming-in-prior-issued-patent-is-rebuttable
rubrics_metrics.description: An inference of abandonment (intent to dedicate to the public) from subject matter disclosed but not claimed in a previously issued patent is rebuttable by filing an application at any time before a statutory bar arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) based solely on issuance of a patent that discloses but does not claim the subject matter is improper if there is copendency between the application and the application that issued as the patent (In re Gibbs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay-in-reapplying-after-abandonment-does-not-necessarily-establish-abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay in reapplying for patent after abandonment of a previous application does not by itself establish abandonment unless there is evidence of expressed intent or conduct by the inventor to abandon the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law shows mere delay is insufficient; context and inventor conduct matter (Petersen v. Fee Int’l, Ltd.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Only-priority-contests-can-let-lapse-of-time-bar-patent (relation-to-102(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere lapse of time will not bar a patent; the exception is when there is a priority contest under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) and the applicant abandons, suppresses, or conceals the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment, suppression, and concealment are treated under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g). See Panduit Corp. v. Dennison Mfg. Co. and MPEP § 2138.03 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition-of-‘patented’-for-102(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be 'patented' an exclusionary right must be formally awarded to the applicant — a formal bestowal of patent rights from the sovereign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gebrauchsmuster (petty patent) can be treated as a patent for 102(d) purposes even if term/duration differ, as long as exclusionary rights are granted (case citations: In re Monks; American Infra-Red Radiant Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Published-application-is-not-a-‘patent’-for-102(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A published or laid-open application is not a 'patent' for purposes of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases include Ex parte Fujishiro (Japanese utility model laid open/kokai), Ex parte Links (German Offenlegungsschriften). Publication without grant does not equate to grant for 102(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed-application-published-for-opposition-may-be-treated-as-patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An examined application that has been allowed and published for opposition may be considered a 'patent' for 102(d) as of the date published for opposition if substantial provisional enforcement rights arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: German Auslegeschrift publication begins opposition period and grants provisional patent rights similar to those after grant; such publication can have legal effect of a patent for 102(d) (Ex parte Beik).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant-occurs-when-patent-becomes-enforceable
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant critical date of a foreign patent for 102(d) purposes is the date the patent becomes enforceable (issued, sealed, or granted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Monks: e.g., British patent reference becomes available as prior art on the sealing date because the right to exclude attaches then.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy-after-grant-does-not-defeat-102(d)-applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: A period of secrecy after granting the patent (e.g., Belgian/Spanish secrecy) does not prevent the patent from being usable in rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as of the grant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Kathawala and older cases: the grant date is the relevant date even if publication is later; secrecy option exercised by patentee does not alter 102(d) effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed-reference-types-for-pre-AIA-35-U.S.C.-102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: A potential reference usable under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) must be a U.S. patent, a U.S. application publication (35 U.S.C. 122(b)), or a WIPO publication of an international application under PCT Article 21(2) in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 102(e) is mainly used when publication/issue dates are too recent for application under 102(a)/(b). Examiner must verify the reference type before applying under 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine-102(e)-date-for-references-not-resulting-from-international-application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the potential reference did not result from, nor claimed the benefit of, an international application, its pre-AIA 102(e) date is its earliest effective U.S. filing date, taking into account any proper benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For benefit claims, prior application(s) must properly support the relied-upon subject matter in compliance with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (112(a)). For benefit claims under 119(e), at least one claim of the potential reference must be supported by the provisional's written description to be usable as prior art as of the provisional's filing date (see MPEP § 2136.03 subsection III).

rubrics_metrics.name: International-application-conditions-for-using-international-filing-date-as-102(e)-date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the potential reference resulted from, or claimed the benefit of, an international application (IA), the IA's international filing date is a U.S. pre-AIA 102(e) filing date only if three conditions are met: (a) IA filed on or after November 29, 2000; (b) IA designated the United States; and (c) IA was published by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2) in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these three conditions are satisfied, the IA filing date (or an earlier effective U.S. filing date claimed properly) can be the 102(e) date, provided subject matter is supported under 112/120/119(e) as applicable. If an earlier application is an IA, it must also satisfy the three conditions for its date to be a U.S. filing date for 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: International-application-filed-on-or-after-Nov-29-2000-but-no-US-designation-or-not-published-in-English
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IA was filed on or after November 29, 2000 but did not designate the U.S. or was not published in English under PCT Art.21(2), do not treat the international filing date as a U.S. filing date for 102(e) purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that case, do not apply the reference as of its international filing date or 371(c) completion date; the reference may be applied under 102(a) or 102(b) as of its publication date, or under 102(e) as of any later U.S. filing date of an application that properly claimed the benefit of the IA.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-application-filed-prior-to-Nov-29-2000 (former-rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IA's international filing date is prior to November 29, 2000, apply pre-AIPA provisions: for U.S. patents, apply 102(e) as of the earlier of the date of completion of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2),(4) or the filing date of the later-filed U.S. application that claimed benefit; for U.S. and WIPO application publications directly resulting from such IA, never apply under 102(e) but apply under 102(a) or 102(b) as of publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application publications of IA filed prior to Nov 29, 2000 have no 102(e) date; patents may have 102(e) date as of fulfillment of 371 requirements (examples in MPEP § 2136).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-priority-dates-claimed-via-35-U.S.C.-119-or-365-cannot-be-used-as-102(e)-dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign application filing dates that are claimed (via 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d),(f) or 365(a) or (b)) in applications which have been published as U.S. or WIPO application publications or patented in the U.S. may not be used as pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) dates for prior art purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes international filing dates claimed as foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 365(a) or (b); examiners must not convert such foreign dates into 102(e) dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit-claims-and-written-description-support-requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For any benefit claim relied upon to establish an earlier 102(e) date (including 119(e), 120, 365(c), 386(c)), the subject matter used in the rejection must be disclosed in the earlier-filed application in compliance with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (112(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically for 119(e) provisional claims, at least one claim of the potential reference must be supported by the provisional application’s written description in compliance with 112 (see MPEP § 2136.03 subsection III). If benefit/priority is improperly claimed or lacks support, the earlier date cannot be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners-follow-stepwise-guidelines-and-examples-to-determine-102(e)-date
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must determine the appropriate pre-AIA 102(e) date for each potential reference by following the guidelines, examples, and flow charts in the section: (A) verify reference type; (B) check if reference resulted from/claimed benefit of IA; (C) if IA involved, evaluate the IA conditions and subrules; (D) be aware of exceptions where publication/issue dates may give earlier 102(a)/(b) dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP provides nine illustrative examples covering common factual situations (Examples 1–9) to aid examiners in applying these rules. Examiners should consider international vs. U.S. filing/claim chains and applicable case law when assigning prior-art dates.
